parsed.explanation: The quoted pruning/contraction passage is indeed terse, but the objection's decisive claim — that the blocker fact 'is false' — is unsupported and, on inspection, wrong. A pairwise-intersecting family of finite sets with a member C of size r genuinely has only finitely many inclusion-minimal transversals (a standard result; attempts to build infinitely many fail, e.g. any candidate minimal transversal must meet C, and the essential-witness sets F_x with F_x ∩ X = {x} force the recursive finiteness). The objector offers no counterexample: no concrete family satisfying the hypotheses with infinitely many minimal transversals, nor a precise identification of a circular inference. The tree argument in the text — finite branching, König's lemma on an infinite branch, some c ∈ C lying in infinitely many selected sets F_k making later selected elements dispensable, contradicting retention of minimal-transversal branches — is compressed but its logic is sound when unpacked, not circular. Since the lemma is true and the proof strategy valid, the objection fails.
